label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly good conditions up at SSV on Wolverine, if you're willing to shlep up the road. HS 50cm with 10-15cm ski pen. Boot pen to ground in most spots.  The mid pack is supportive. Was able to skin from below G-eye.  Observed a fair number of sz 2 on solar aspects starting in alpine going nearly full path. Ice climbers take note.

reports.title: Quartz Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing conditions with little wind affect to the recent HN. No avalanches observed.

reports.title: Simpson Pass
reports.comment: quick: Pretty much as the bulletin suggested. We were able to trigger  some unsupported East facing layers with little effort.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Pretty much exactly as advertised in Saturday's bulletin.  Best riding to be had at and below tree line in sheltered zones.  Wind hammered in the alpine, blown down to rock in windward aspects on Twin Cairns.  Light snow all day with moderate westerlies, heavy snow came in around 3pm as we were pulling out - 3cm on the truck in 20 mins.

reports.title: Quartz Hill - Sunchine slack country
reports.comment: quick: Dropped in the NE aspect of Quartz Hill in Sunshine slackcountry today. Very stable conditions. Still early season so had to watch for shark fins - but great powder to be had. Not much cornice growth despite the winds and the little there was was quite consolidated. Nothing exciting to report actually ...

reports.title: Goat's Eye Profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Profile taken at treeline (2200 m) on Goat's Eye mountain. The snowpack is growing weaker each day with these cold temperatures, and you can see in this profile that the entire snowpack is now faceted. Note the strong temperature gradient in the upper half of the snowpack, which is driving vapor up and out of the snowpack rapidly and creating the conditions for the Loose Dry facet avalan…

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: snowpack: Sudden planar CTE4 down 25cm, secondary uneven break CTH25 down 40cm. Wind slab was extremely variable.

reports.title: Bourgeau meadows
reports.comment: quick: The mid-pack was generally supportive. Near rocks and trees and thin spots you would collapse into the bottomless facets.   Had one whumpf on a south aspect at 2250m on the transition from wind blown ridge to well supported good coverage run.

reports.title: Sunshine Meadows
reports.comment: snowpack: 25* slope, SW. CTM7 60cm down, drop. CTH3 35cm down, sudden planar.

reports.title: Wawa Ridge - North Aspect - Treeline Test Profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Ski quality was good, firmer under foot than we were expecting in thicker areas on the north aspect

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly good skiing up on little Quartz with fast and buttery turns over a supportive midpack.  Observed shooting cracks on thin and hard slab areas.  A ski sluff on a small convexity propagated 10m in the upper 10cm of wind sift, but otherwise no recent avalanche activity observed.

reports.title: Sunshine slackcountry - extensive remote triggering
reports.comment: quick: Saw significant remote triggering activity in Sunshine Meadows on countless convex rolls while heading towards Dinosaur Head / Healy seconday drain. Conditions were highly variable - from bottomless facets to P windslab. Must've seen at least 6 occurences of remote triggering which made for a great outdoor classroom for a 10yr old. All occurences were N aspect around 2330m, involved convex …

reports.title: Inbounds Sunshine Village
reports.comment: quick: Riding in-bounds and triggered a small size 1 avalanche off the skiers right of Wawa Chair - Understandably so, due to the major high-speed winds loading 10cm of fresh onto north-eastern slopes, and the steepness of the slope. But either way, it strengthened my decision to stay in-bounds for the afternoon rather than ski the twins or wawa ridge.

reports.title: Full Profile Goat's Eye Study Plot
reports.comment: snowpack: Did 5 compression tests : Easy results of a Progressive Compression Character down 20 cm on small surface hoar. Moderate x1 and Hard x 4 results down 60 cm Sudden Collapse in facets. Propagation saw test x 3 - one 25cm to end and two 30cm slab fractures. No question that there is a weak layer: it is the slab above this that is making things so variable!

reports.title: Healy Pass off Wawa Ridge
reports.comment:
avalanche: Skier remote triggered, size 2 to 2.5 avalanche at tree line on Healy Pass. Avalanche crown on slope convexity, propagating approximately 100m across to ground (1.5m deep) and running ~150m.  Boarder near tree line (lookers left of slope) with crown initiating ~30m above. Variable snowpack thickness nearing rock outcrops (right). No injuries but close call. 

Touchy conditions, hindsigh…

reports.title: Rock Isle Lake - sunshine slackcountry
reports.comment: quick: Hot lapped Rock Isle lake all day today - great snow although it was getting heavier by the time we left at 2pm. Dig a pit on NW aspect near a wind affected ridge at 2268m  - 165cm HS, got CTM18 SC down 120cm on depth hoar (repeatable). Didn't bother with an ECT but would've been interesting. Wasn't entirely surprised given the rocky terrain underneath and the location - but took it easy an…

reports.title: Goat's Eye Study Plot Full Profile
reports.comment: snowpack: One resistant planar result in compression tests at 30cm hard range. Facets / depth hoar  react consistently in the moderate range as a sudden collapse when the top 40cm is removed 55cm from the ground. Noticeable settlement in the midpack since last visit two weeks ago.
